lesson: Grant Abbitt detailed sword topology and hard-surface workflow

strengths: Blade is one connected 72-vertex, 70-face, all-quad manifold shell with a modeled center ridge.
A render-driven correction lengthened and slimmed the cage rather than hiding the mismatch with shading.
Semantic ridge and outline creases control one live, unapplied Subdivision Surface modifier.
The fitted hilt is one connected 12-sided revolved cage; it is separate from the blade at a justified assembly boundary.
Fresh Blender 5.2 evaluation reports 280 all-quad, manifold faces and zero pinch candidates.
limitations: The shoulder transition is blockier and less integrated than the creator target.
The long blade arc and upswept tip remain only approximate.
The hilt is straight and simplified compared with the subtly curved, more detailed target.
The reproduction captures the construction principle but not enough shape fidelity for the 8/10 I0 gate.

transfer.result: The connected silhouette-plus-ridge shell transferred to a leaf spearhead with 42 vertices, 40 quad faces, zero non-manifold edges, zero n-gons and zero degenerate faces.
transfer.rejected_attempt: Collapsing three tip vertices to one coordinate produced two degenerate quads; the tip was rebuilt as a tiny three-vertex termination before acceptance.

promoted_rule: For thin ridged weapons, build one connected front/rear quad shell from silhouette and ridge paths; preserve sharp intent with selective creases and live SubD, and never collapse a quad row into a coincident multi-vertex tip.
next_lesson_gate: Do not advance to I1. Select another bounded, weapon-relevant intermediate tutorial whose creator result is independently visible and target an 8/10 reproduction.
